title: An information integration theory of consciousness
authors: Tononi G.
relevance_note: Founding paper of IIT: consciousness = integrated information, Phi via minimum-information bipartition and effective information. Conceptual anchor for modeling aging as erosion of a network's integrated information.

title: Measuring information integration
authors: Tononi G.; Sporns O.
relevance_note: First computable integration metrics (effective information, bipartitions) applicable to real connectivity matrices. Direct ancestor of our network-degradation Phi computations.

title: Integrated Information in Discrete Dynamical Systems: Motivation and Theoretical Framework
authors: Balduzzi D.; Tononi G.
relevance_note: Extends Phi to discrete Markov dynamical systems and defines the main complex. Needed to treat coupled neural/bioelectric units as time-evolving systems rather than static graphs.

title: From the Phenomenology to the Mechanisms of Consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0
authors: Oizumi M.; Albantakis L.; Tononi G.
relevance_note: IIT 3.0: Phi as irreducible cause-effect structure (cause-effect repertoires). Defines the modern Phi our approximations proxy; motivates approximations since exact Phi is super-exponentially hard.

title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: Formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
authors: Albantakis L; Barbosa L; Findlay G; et al.; Tononi G
relevance_note: Current canonical IIT formulation (intrinsic existence, cause-effect power, intrinsic irreducibility). The formal reference for what our computable proxies approximate. First author Albantakis; Tononi last author; PLOS Comput Biol 2023.

title: A measure for intrinsic information
authors: Barbosa L. S.; Marshall W.; Streipert S.; Albantakis L.; Tononi G.
relevance_note: Introduces Phi_R, a tractable intrinsic-information measure via soft (Lebesgue-uniform) perturbations. One of the best candidate Phi approximations to implement directly on coupled systems. Note exact title 'A measure for intrinsic information', year 2020.

title: Mechanism Integrated Information
authors: Barbosa L. S.; Marshall W.; Albantakis L.; Tononi G.
relevance_note: Mechanism Integrated Information (MII): irreducibility of small mechanisms rather than whole systems. Useful for node-level integration accounting in the aging network model.

title: PyPhi: A toolbox for integrated information theory
authors: Mayner WGP; Marshall W; Albantakis L; et al.; Tononi G
relevance_note: PyPhi: reference open-source implementation of IIT 3.0 Phi for discrete Markov systems. Natural benchmark/validation target for custom Phi approximation code.

title: Practical Measures of Integrated Information for Time-Series Data
authors: Barrett A. B.; Seth A. K.
relevance_note: THE paper for Gaussian-linear Phi: derives Phi_EI and Phi_ar for multivariate Gaussian systems via Granger-style effective information, with estimation-bias caveats. Core reference for our linear-system Phi implementation.

title: Unified framework for information integration based on information geometry
authors: Oizumi M.; Tsuchiya N.; Amari S.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 113(51):14817-14822
relevance_note: Information-geometric integration measures (Phi* family) with analytic Gaussian-system treatment. A second, geometry-grounded route to linear-system Phi.

title: A general spectral decomposition of causal influences applied to integrated information
authors: Cohen D.; Sasai S.; Tsuchiya N.; Oizumi M.
relevance_note: Spectral decomposition of causal influences (Oizumi lab) for linear dynamical models. Practical route to frequency-resolved integration measures for time-series/network models of aging bioelectric systems.

title: Measuring Integrated Information: Comparison of Candidate Measures in Theory and Simulation
authors: Mediano P.; Seth A.; Barrett A.
relevance_note: Systematic comparison of candidate integrated-information measures in theory and simulation. Use to choose which Phi proxy to adopt and avoid known degeneracies (e.g., feedforward chains).

title: The strength of weak integrated information theory
authors: Mediano P. A.; Rosas F. E.; Bor D.; Seth A. K.; Barrett A. B.
relevance_note: 'Weak IIT': integrated-information measures as empirically useful descriptors without IIT's ontological commitments. The correct epistemic stance for an aging-modeling project that computes Phi instrumentally.

title: Toward a unified taxonomy of information dynamics via Integrated Information Decomposition
authors: Mediano P. A. M.; Rosas F. E.; Luppi A. I.; Carhart-Harris R. L.; Bor D.; Seth A. K.; Barrett A. B.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(39):e2423297122
relevance_note: Published, citable form of integrated information decomposition (PhiID): decomposes integration into redundant/unique/synergistic parts. Ideal for quantifying which kind of integration aging destroys first.

title: Improved Measures of Integrated Information
authors: Tegmark M
relevance_note: Tegmark's improved/approximate Phi measures with numerical optimization. Additional toolbox for tractable Phi on larger networks.

title: Computing Integrated Information (Phi) in Discrete Dynamical Systems with Multi-Valued Variables
authors: Gomez C; Mayner WGP; Beheler-Amass T; Tononi G; Albantakis L
relevance_note: Exact Phi computation for multi-valued (non-binary) discrete systems. Relevant if bioelectric units carry graded states (e.g., discretized membrane-voltage levels).

title: The unfolding argument: Why IIT and other causal structure theories cannot explain consciousness
authors: Doerig A; Schurger A; Hess S; Herzog MH
relevance_note: The unfolding argument: causal-structure theories like IIT are insensitive to isomorphic network unfoldings. The sharpest principled falsifiability critique; cite for honest framing. (No paper titled 'unfalsifiability of IIT' exists - this is the actual critique.)

title: Hard criteria for empirical theories of consciousness
authors: Doerig A; Schurger A; Herzog MH
relevance_note: Sets empirical/falsifiability criteria for theories of consciousness and evaluates IIT's shortfalls. Pairs with the unfolding argument for balanced treatment of IIT's scientific status.

title: The Integrated Information Theory of Consciousness as Pseudoscience
authors: Fleming SM; Frith CD; Goodale M; et al. (open letter, 100+ signatories)
relevance_note: Open letter (100+ signatories incl. Fleming, Frith, Goodale, Lau) arguing IIT's central claims drift into pseudoscience. Strongest public criticism; must be acknowledged in any Phi-based project framing.

title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
authors: Cogitate Consortium; Ferrante O; Gorska-Klimowska U; et al. (incl. Tononi G, Mudrik L, Melloni L)
relevance_note: First preregistered adversarial head-to-head test of IIT vs global neuronal workspace (humans, NHP, mice); several IIT predictions unsupported. State-of-the-art empirical grounding for IIT's contested status.

title: Protocol for testing global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness in non-human primates and mice
authors: Gibbons M; McBride EG; et al.
relevance_note: Preregistered animal-model protocol of the adversarial collaboration. Methodological template for empirical validation of Phi-style measures in coupled biological systems.

title: XXIV. On the nature of the function expressive of the law of human mortality, and on a new mode of determining the value of life contingencies. In a letter to Francis Baily, Esq. F. R. S. &c
authors: Gompertz B.
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London (115):513-583
relevance_note: The original Gompertz law: human mortality hazard grows ~exponentially with age. The central empirical law our network-degradation model must derive.

title: On the Law of Mortality and the Construction of Annuity Tables
authors: Makeham W. M.
venue: The Assurance Magazine and Journal of the Institute of Actuaries 8(6):301-310
relevance_note: Makeham's extension adding the age-independent hazard term (Gompertz-Makeham). The standard baseline mortality model for fitting our simulated hazard curves.

title: A Statistical Distribution Function of Wide Applicability
authors: Weibull W.
relevance_note: The Weibull distribution: canonical reliability-engineering hazard model (power-law hazard). The competing null model to Gompertz when fitting hazards from degrading redundant networks.

title: The analysis of survival (mortality) data: Fitting Gompertz, Weibull, and logistic functions
authors: Wilson D. L.
relevance_note: Practical comparison of fitting Gompertz, Weibull, and logistic mortality functions. Model-selection template for our simulated survival data.

title: Biological Implications of the Weibull and Gompertz Models of Aging
authors: Ricklefs R. E.; Scheuerlein A.
venue: The Journals of Gerontology Series A: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences 57(2):B69-B76
relevance_note: Biological interpretation of Weibull vs Gompertz fits (initial vulnerability vs actuarial senescence). Supplies interpretive logic for whichever law redundancy-depletion produces.

title: The Reliability Theory of Aging and Longevity
authors: GAVRILOV L. A.; GAVRILOVA N. S.
relevance_note: CRITICAL: derives Gompertz-like exponentially increasing failure rates from systems of redundant, non-aging elements whose redundancy is progressively exhausted; also derives Weibull regimes and late-life plateaus. The mathematical template for deriving Gompertz from information-network redundancy depletion.

title: Evolution of ageing
authors: Kirkwood T. B. L.
relevance_note: Disposable soma theory: maintenance-vs-reproduction trade-off explains why somatic information integrity is allowed to decay. Evolutionary grounding for imperfect bioelectric/genomic repair.

title: The temporal scaling of Caenorhabditis elegans ageing
authors: Stroustrup N; Anthony WE; Nash ZM; et al.
relevance_note: C. elegans lifespan interventions act by uniform temporal rescaling of a single aging program. Consistent with aging being dominated by few effective dimensions (e.g., one integration-loss variable); our Phi-decline model should reproduce this scaling.

title: Biodemographic Trajectories of Longevity
authors: Vaupel JW; Carey JR; Christensen K; et al.
relevance_note: Biodemographic synthesis documenting late-life mortality deceleration and plateaus across species. The high-age phenomenon our redundancy-exhaustion model must reproduce.

title: Slowing of Mortality Rates at Older Ages in Large Medfly Cohorts
authors: Carey J. R.; Liedo P.; Orozco D.; Vaupel J. W.
relevance_note: Large medfly cohorts show mortality slowing/decline at extreme ages. Key empirical constraint (deceleration beyond Gompertz) for redundancy-exhaustion models.

title: The Hallmarks of Aging
authors: López-Otín C.; Blasco M. A.; Partridge L.; Serrano M.; Kroemer G.
relevance_note: Canonical catalog of aging hallmarks. Maps abstract 'information-integrity loss' onto concrete biology (genomic instability, epigenetic alterations, proteostasis loss).

title: Hallmarks of aging: An expanding universe
authors: López-Otín C.; Blasco M. A.; Partridge L.; Serrano M.; Kroemer G.
relevance_note: Updated hallmarks framework (12 hallmarks) foregrounding information/epigenetic deregulation. Biological grounding for the information-loss framing. DOI ends .001 (not .002).

title: Loss of epigenetic information as a cause of mammalian aging
authors: Yang J; Hayano M; Griffin PT; et al.; Sinclair DA
relevance_note: Flagship information-theoretic aging result: aging as loss of epigenetic information, partially reversible by OSK reprogramming (incl. epigenetic noise/reversibility assays). The direct biological analog of our Phi-decline hypothesis.

title: Loss of 'Complexity' and Aging
authors: Lipsitz LA; Goldberger AL
api_source: crossref+pubmed (PMID 1482430 used to complete author list)
relevance_note: Classic statement that aging is a loss of physiological complexity (fractal/dynamical metrics decline). Dynamical-systems precursor to measuring information-integration decline with age.

title: What is physiologic complexity and how does it change with aging and disease?
authors: Goldberger A. L.; Peng C.; Lipsitz L. A.
relevance_note: Sharpens the physiologic-complexity thesis and its mechanisms. Bridges the 1992 JAMA paper to concrete time-series complexity metrics computable alongside Phi.

title: Increased cell-to-cell variation in gene expression in ageing mouse heart
authors: Bahar R; Hartmann CH; Rodriguez KA; et al.
relevance_note: Aging increases cell-to-cell gene-expression variance (mouse heart). Direct evidence that aging destabilizes expression attractors (noise up = cellular information integrity down).

title: Aging increases cell-to-cell transcriptional variability upon immune stimulation
authors: Martinez-Jimenez CP; Eling N; Chen H; et al.
relevance_note: Single-cell RNA-seq quantification of aging-driven transcriptional variability upon immune stimulation. Modern attractor-destabilization evidence and a quantitative target for the noise-growth term.

title: Epigenetic gambling and epigenetic drift as an antagonistic pleiotropic mechanism of aging
authors: Martin G. M.
relevance_note: Frames stochastic epigenetic drift as an antagonistic-pleiotropic aging mechanism. Theoretical bridge between information-theoretic noise accumulation and phenotypic aging.

title: In Vivo Amelioration of Age-Associated Hallmarks by Partial Reprogramming
authors: Ocampo A; Reddy P; Martinez-Redondo P; et al.; Izpisua Belmonte JC
relevance_note: Cyclic OSK partial reprogramming ameliorates multiple aging hallmarks in vivo. Demonstrates reversibility of epigenetic/informational drift, motivating a 'rejuvenation = restore Phi' intervention arm. Published in Cell (not Nature).

title: Long-term meditators self-induce high-amplitude gamma synchrony during mental practice
authors: Lutz A.; Greischar L. L.; Rawlings N. B.; Ricard M.; Davidson R. J.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 101(46):16369-16373
relevance_note: Long-term meditators self-induce high-amplitude gamma synchrony. Canonical evidence that mental training upregulates large-scale neural integration - the 'increase Phi' arm of the project.

title: Alterations in Brain and Immune Function Produced by Mindfulness Meditation
authors: Davidson R. J.; Kabat-Zinn J.; Schumacher J.; Rosenkranz M.; Muller D.; Santorelli S. F.; Urbanowski F.; Harrington A.; Bonus K.; Sheridan J. F.
relevance_note: 8-week mindfulness training changed prefrontal EEG asymmetry AND immune function (vaccine antibody titers). Cleanest classic evidence for a trainable brain-to-body (consciousness-physiology) interface.

title: Well–being and affective style: neural substrates and biobehavioural correlates
authors: Davidson R. J.
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B: Biological Sciences 359(1449):1395-1411
relevance_note: Framework linking affective style and well-being to prefrontal/limbic circuit function. Psychological-level correlate that integration-based biomarkers must relate to. (Phil Trans B 2004, not PNAS.)

title: The neuroscience of mindfulness meditation
authors: Tang Y.; Hölzel B. K.; Posner M. I.
relevance_note: Authoritative review of mindfulness-meditation neuroscience (attention, body awareness, emotion regulation, self-perception). The framing document for meditation as trainable neural integration.

title: Meditation states and traits: EEG, ERP, and neuroimaging studies.
authors: Cahn B. R.; Polich J.
relevance_note: Comprehensive review of meditation EEG/ERP/neuroimaging states vs traits. Methodological reference for electrophysiological coherence/integration measures to compare against Phi estimates.

title: Bioelectric signaling: Reprogrammable circuits underlying embryogenesis, regeneration, and cancer
authors: Levin M.
relevance_note: Bioelectric circuits (ion-channel/voltage networks) store and process morphogenetic information reprogrammably. Defines the bioelectric control-network substrate of the aging model.

title: Information integration during bioelectric regulation of morphogenesis of the embryonic frog brain
authors: Manicka S.; Pai V. P.; Levin M.
relevance_note: Computes IIT-style integrated information over bioelectric state-transition models of frog embryonic morphogenesis. The closest existing precedent to our coupled bioelectric Phi computations.
